US-TN.cite: 2020 Tenn. Pub. Acts ch. 591 (SB 1934), amending Tenn. Code Ann. titles 5, 6, 7, 65 and 68
US-TN.note: Public Chapter 591 bars political subdivisions from prohibiting a utility connection based on the type or source of energy delivered.

US-OK.note: No city, town or county may adopt building or construction rules restricting or prohibiting connections to lawful utility providers; the act took effect 11/1/2020.

US-LA.note: No parish or municipality may adopt a code or land-use rule restricting a person from using a capable, authorized utility provider; Act 46 took effect 8/1/2020.

US-ID.note: HB 106 (2023), Session Law ch. 55, bars counties and cities from prohibiting an energy utility connection or restricting its fuel source, effective 7/1/2023.

US-GA.note: No governmental entity may adopt a policy that prohibits utility or gas connections based on the type or source of energy or fuel; the act took effect on the governor's approval on 5/6/2021 (per the National Propane Gas Association).

US-MS.cite: Miss. HB 632 (2021), the "All Fuels Act of 2021"
US-MS.note: No political subdivision may prohibit the connection or reconnection of a service based on the type or source of energy; the governor approved it 3/17/2021 and it took effect on passage.

US-IN.note: Counties, cities and towns may not bar a utility from serving, or a customer from connecting to, a utility service based on its energy source; the governor signed HEA 1191 on 4/29/2021 (the exact effective date was not read).

US-AL.note: Alabama HB 446 bars governmental entities from prohibiting use of an authorized utility service, and the governor signed it 5/3/2021; the Act number, code section and effective date were not read from a state page.

US-WI.cite: Wis. 2023 SB 49 (proposed Wis. Stat. § 66.04045, not enacted)
US-WI.note: The Legislature passed a bill barring local limits on utility service by energy source, but the governor vetoed it and the override failed 5/15/2024, so no preemption is in force.

US-SC.note: No statewide ban, and the local-government provisions of S.C. Code tit. 6 contain no energy-choice or fuel-source preemption; the multistate tracker lists no South Carolina bill passed.

US-DC.note: The 2022 act requires net-zero-energy building rules by 12/31/2026 (and bars permits after that date under Appendix Z if the Mayor misses it), so no gas ban was in force on 1/1/2026 and the District has no separate local layer to preempt.

US-PR.note: No territorial law banning gas hookups in new buildings or barring local governments from doing so was found for Puerto Rico, and the multistate tracker lists none.

US-GU.note: No territorial law banning gas hookups in new buildings or barring local governments from doing so was found for Guam, and the multistate tracker lists none.

US-MP.note: No territorial law banning gas hookups in new buildings or barring local governments from doing so was found for the Northern Mariana Islands, and the multistate tracker lists none.

US-TX.cite: Tex. Loc. Gov't Code ch. 211 (2025 S.B. 15 and S.B. 840)
US-TX.note: Weak: Texas S.B. 15 (2025) allows single-family homes on 3,000-square-foot lots in new subdivisions and S.B. 840 allows apartments in commercial zones, but neither requires duplexes on existing single-family lots.

US-UT.note: Utah H.B. 37 (2025) only authorizes cities and counties to allow more density in exchange for affordability terms, and no state law requires duplexes or more on single-family lots.

US-CT.note: Connecticut H.B. 8002 (signed 11/26/2025) rewards towns that add housing near transit and downtowns but leaves residential zoning to each town, so no state law requires duplexes on single-family lots.

US-FL.note: Weak: Florida law requires multifamily housing only in commercial, industrial and mixed-use zones (Live Local Act), and no state law requires duplexes on single-family lots.

US-GU.note: Guam's zoning law permits only one-family dwellings (and accessory units) by right in the R1 zone, and duplexes there need conditional-use approval.

US-AS.note: American Samoa's single dwelling (R1) zone permits only one-family dwellings and their accessory uses, so duplexes are not allowed by right there.

US-VI.cite: V.I. Code tit. 29, § 228 (table of permitted uses, R-1)
US-VI.note: The territorial zoning table lets two-family dwellings be built as of right in the R-1 low-density residential zone beside single-family homes, and it has no single-family-only zone (read from the 2019 codification).
